content: Acebutolol is a medication prescribed to treat irregular heartbeats. It functions by relaxing blood vessels and slowing the heart rate, which improves blood flow and reduces blood pressure. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Acebutolol is available in capsule form and is taken orally, typically once or twice a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take acebutolol exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. This medication helps control your condition but does not cure it. Continue taking acebutolol even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Acebutolol is sometimes used to treat chest pain (angina). Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. Before taking acebutolol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to acebutolol or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially those for migraines, diabetes, asthma, allergies, colds, pain, high blood pressure, or heart disease, as well as reserpine and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had heart, kidney, or liver disease; asthma or other lung diseases; blood vessel disorders; severe allergies; diabetes; or an overactive thyroid gland. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking acebutolol, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform the doctor or dentist that you are taking acebutolol. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can increase the drowsiness caused by this medication. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking acebutolol. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Acebutolol may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience dizziness, lightheadedness, excessive tiredness, headache, constipation, diarrhea, upset stomach, or muscle aches, especially if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience shortness of breath, wheezing, swelling of the feet or lower legs, or chest pain. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your blood pressure should be monitored regularly to assess your response to acebutolol. Your doctor may ask you to check your pulse (heart rate). Ask your doctor or pharmacist to teach you how to do this. If your pulse is faster or slower than it should be, contact your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. It is important to maintain a written list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including vitamins, minerals, and dietary supplements. Bring this list with you to every doctor’s visit or if you are admitted to a hospital. This information is also crucial in case of emergencies.
